title: AI Media and Visual Repository
answer: Keynotes, conference talks, tutorials, podcasts with transcripts, and a diagram and image library.

reading.body:
The repository is a curated index of 18 items across three sections: video, podcasts, and images and diagrams. It is a catalog of pointers, not a store of content.

The three sections split by medium rather than by subject. Video covers vendor keynotes, conference talks, lecture series, and explainers. Podcasts are tracked by host, focus, and whether transcripts exist. The image library covers architecture diagrams, illustrated walkthroughs, and browser-based model explorers. The counts are small and uneven: 7 videos, 6 podcasts, 5 image sets.

For AI specifically, the useful distinction is between announcements and explanation. Vendor keynotes are where model and hardware claims are made public, and the data treats them as a category worth watching. The diagram and image section is the one that touches how systems are actually built, since architecture diagrams and model explorers describe structure rather than narrate it. Nothing here measures compute, power, or buildings, and the data does not claim to.

What the data does not tell you: it holds no episode feed, no download or view counts, no ranking, and no dates for individual items. The counts describe how many entries each section curates, not how much material exists or how current it is. A reader cannot infer from this whether any listed talk or diagram is still accurate.
